description: Five files declare the toolchain and tests/test_toolchain_versions.py fails the build if they ever disagree. That test is a safety net only while Renovate can (a) see every declaration and (b) move them all in one pull request. Miss either and it becomes a tripwire: the next Python patch bumps the Dockerfile, leaves .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml behind, and the test blocks the PR.

(a) Visibility. The dockerfile, docker-compose and npm managers are enabled by default, so Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml and frontend/package.json are already read. The workflow's PYTHON_VERSION, NODE_VERSION and POSTGRES_VERSION are plain `env:` values that no manager reads; the `# renovate:` comments above them are parsed only by the custom manager that customManagers:githubActionsVersions installs, and that is a preset, not a default. Its managerFilePatterns cover `.forgejo/workflows`, so ci.yml is in scope.

pyproject.toml's requires-python has no Renovate manager at all and stays a manual edit. The agreement test derives the expected value from the Dockerfile, so patch bumps stay green and only a minor bump needs that edit.
(b) Grouping is keyed on the dependency, never on the datasource -- see the packageRules below.
Dockerfile's `FROM python:` and ci.yml's PYTHON_VERSION are one decision, so they belong in one PR. Split across two, either PR alone fails test_ci_tests_the_python_the_image_ships.

Node is why these rules match on the dependency name rather than the datasource. It is reported under datasource `docker` from the Dockerfile's `FROM node:` and from the annotated NODE_VERSION, but under datasource `node-version` from frontend/package.json's `engines.node` -- the npm manager maps engines.node to the node-version datasource. A group keyed on matchDatasources: ["docker"] would therefore leave engines.node behind in a second PR, and either PR alone fails test_package_json_pins_node_exactly.

depName is the same bare string in all three: the dockerfile manager reports the image name without registry or tag, the npm manager reports the key from `engines`, and the custom manager reports whatever the annotation's depName= says. matchDepNames is what unifies them.

docker-compose.yml's postgres image and ci.yml's POSTGRES_VERSION, which the workflow's `docker run` lines all reference. The developer database and the database CI verifies migrations against have to be the same server.
